newsitem.title: TANZANIA: U.N. Rwanda trial witness says daughter raped.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Rwanda trial witness says daughter raped.

text.p: A witness told on Monday a U.N. tribunal on Rwanda that her six-year-old daughter was raped by three men sent to her house by a former Hutu mayor on trial for genocide.
The Tutsi witness known as "J" to protect her identity said her father, brother, daughter and mother were all killed during massacres at central Taba commune.

Jean-Paul Akayesu, 43, stands accused of directing the Taba massacres and has pleaded not guilty to charges of genocide and crimes against humanity. If convicted he will face life imprisonment, the tribunal's highest penalty.
"They raped my six-year-old daughter when they came to kill my father," witness "J" said of the three men.
"They arrived with machetes and guns, searched the house and took us with them to the commune office where I met Akayesu and other police officers," she said.
She said her mother and child were killed and their bodies dumped in a pit latrine, while her brother was beaten to death at a mass grave, adding she did not actually see the killings.
The witness said she was forced to climb up a tree and hide for a week coming down only at night to avoid capture, despite being six months pregnant.

Akayesu is the first to stand trial before the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR) set up in November 1994 to bring to justice the central architects of the genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
Presiding Judge Laity Kama of Senegal adjourned the session until Tuesday when the court will hear from its 15th witness.
